about: Weingut Stefan Müller is a family estate in Krettnach, a village in the Konzer Tälchen, a small side valley of the Saar just before the river joins the Mosel near Trier. The family farms about 10 hectares, roughly 90 percent Riesling with a little Pinot Noir and Pinot Blanc, and the estate is now in its third generation under Stefan Müller. Alongside better-known Saar names such as Zilliken, he has helped bring overlooked parcels back into focus, and his labels carry topographic maps of each vineyard.

Niedermenniger Herrenberg is a red-slate site in the neighboring village of Niedermennig; this wine comes from a single parcel planted in 1969, and the village’s parcels include many old, ungrafted vines. Grapes are picked by hand, fermented with wild yeast and never chaptalized, and each wine stays in the tank or old barrel where it began fermenting until it is finished, with sulfur added only at bottling. The vineyards are farmed without herbicides or insecticides, with fungicide used only when a vintage demands it.

Feinherb is the German term for an off-dry style. About 25 grams per liter of residual sugar against 9.8 grams of acidity, at around 10 percent alcohol, explains the effect the estate describes: lightly sweet on entry, dry-tasting on the finish, with a light, fresh frame and green-apple, crystalline fruit rather than riper yellow fruit.
